summary: Provider-pluggable model adapter (EU Vertex canonical), private network only.

target.note: server and destination are null on purpose: the reconciler resolves them from the instance and aborts when the match is not unique, rather than guessing.

source.note: The platform repository is private, so Coolify must read it through an installed GitHub App. This instance offers two sources: the built-in 'Public GitHub', which can only read public repositories and so cannot read this one, and the installed App 'adapteng-coolify'. With two candidates the choice is a decision rather than a lookup, so it is declared here where it can be reviewed instead of being inferred at run time.

network.note: public_fqdn is null and must stay null: this service is reachable only from the private Docker network, exactly like adapteng-baserow-adapter. network_aliases is the field that actually makes the service reachable by name, and it is owned here because the API reports it and a write to it can therefore be read back and verified. Measured on 2026-08-12 in run 31590576870: from inside this container, adapteng-baserow-adapter resolved to 10.0.1.11 while ai-gateway did not resolve at all. The container is on the shared network with working embedded DNS; what was missing is a name. Coolify names containers after the application uuid, so without an alias the display name is not a name on the network. adapteng-baserow-adapter carries custom_network_aliases=adapteng-baserow-adapter, which is why it answers and this did not.

health_check.note: enabled false does not mean no health check is wanted. Coolify decides the container probe from this one flag. With enabled true it generates 'curl -s -X GET -f <url> > /dev/null || wget -q -O- <url> > /dev/null || exit 1' and runs it inside the container. This image is python:3.11-slim with system dependencies deliberately kept minimal, so it carries neither curl nor wget: the probe exited 1 every time. Verified on deployment n12qiqlkjcb74u0bakmhtwqz, which logged '/bin/sh: 1: curl: not found' and '/bin/sh: 1: wget: not found' on all five attempts and ended 'New container is not healthy, rolling back to the old container'. Every deployment of this service had failed this way. A custom command is not a way out: Coolify honours health_check_command only when health_check_type is 'cmd', and then filters it against ^[a-zA-Z0-9 \-_./:=@,+]+$, which admits no quotes and no parentheses, so no python -c form can be expressed at all, and a rejected command falls back to the same curl probe with only a warning. The one setting under which Coolify honours the image's own HEALTHCHECK is this flag being false, because Application::parseHealthcheckFromDockerfile records a HEALTHCHECK only when isHealthcheckDisabled() is true. The remaining fields are kept, not deleted, because that same parser overwrites the stored interval, timeout, retries and start period from the HEALTHCHECK directives: these numbers and the image's directives have to agree or reconcile and deploy would overwrite each other on every run.
health_check.container_gate_note: container_gate names what actually gates a rolling update, because 'enabled' does not. Three values are possible. 'coolify_http' is the generated curl/wget probe and requires enabled true. 'image' is a HEALTHCHECK instruction in the service image, requires enabled false, and is a real gate: Coolify logs 'Custom healthcheck found in Dockerfile' and waits for it. 'absent' means no probe runs at all: with enabled false and no HEALTHCHECK in the image, ApplicationDeploymentJob::health_check sets newVersionIsHealthy = true and returns without testing anything. It is 'absent' today, and that is a real and stated loss, not a formality: a container that boots and answers nobody will be promoted. It is recorded here rather than left implicit because this service has already been reported running:healthy for hours while detached from the network, and an unstated missing check is how that happened. Restoring it needs one additive line in Ivan-Shyla/adapteng-automation-platform, services/ai-gateway/Dockerfile, whose directives must carry exactly the four numbers above: HEALTHCHECK --interval=15s --timeout=10s --start-period=30s --retries=5 CMD ["python", "-c", "import sys, urllib.request; sys.exit(0 if urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8081/health', timeout=5).status == 200 else 1)"]. That image already has python and needs no new package, so it costs nothing in supply-chain terms; adding curl would mean an unpinned apt install in an image whose base is digest-pinned and whose wheels are hash-locked. That line landed. Ivan-Shyla/adapteng-automation-platform PR #127, 'Carry the readiness gate in the image, and probe /ready', merged at 23:46:05Z as feee3166, and the directive is on that repository's main at services/ai-gateway/Dockerfile line 67. Its four numbers were checked against this file rather than assumed and carry --interval=15s --timeout=10s --start-period=30s --retries=5, equal to the four above, so the parser that overwrites them has nothing to disagree about. It probes /ready rather than /health, and it is right to: /health answers without touching the database, so gating promotion on it would prove only that a process is listening, which is the failure this service already had. container_gate is therefore 'image' and path is '/ready' as of this edit. How it got there is worth keeping, because the reasoning was wrong twice. #127's only red was root-rollout-tests, a flaky test double, and an earlier version of this note said not to re-run it because that run was the only evidence the re-run remedy can fail. That was wrong about GitHub's data model. Every attempt stays independently addressable at /actions/runs/<id>/attempts/<n> with its own conclusion and its own per-job conclusions, so a re-run rewrites only the run's top-level conclusion, which is merely the field default tooling reads. Tested rather than argued: after re-running 31532517315 to attempt 3 success, attempts 1 and 2 still read failure and attempt 2 still names root-rollout-tests. Nothing was lost and the PR went green. The other error ran the opposite way: this note claimed #127 did not depend on #128 because they are not stacked and #127's own authorization passes, both true, from which the conclusion did not follow, since #128 repairs the very flake that was blocking #127. In the event the re-run settled it without #128, which remains the real fix for the defect.

delivery.note: Deployment is driven only by the deploy operation of this repository's workflow, so a push to the platform repository never releases by itself. force_https is off because there is no public route to redirect.

settings_not_reported_by_api.note: This Coolify instance does not report the four delivery flags on the application resource. Verified on 2026-08-11 against application e13v7c6zjof7dmcpywqbyas3: the list entry and the detail read each carry 93 keys with no settings relation and none of these names, and GET /applications/{uuid}/settings and /advanced both answer 404 while ?include=settings changes nothing. A write that cannot be re-read cannot be verified, so the driver does not write these at all; it reports them for the owner to set in the UI. Every entry here has to state why leaving it unset is safe.

is_auto_deploy_enabled.reason: Not reported and not accepted by the creation endpoint on this version.
is_auto_deploy_enabled.compensating_control: Releases are driven only by the deploy operation of .github/workflows/coolify-deploy.yml, which is workflow_dispatch only. An auto-deploy would redeploy the same declared branch of the same declared repository, so it cannot release unreviewed code from elsewhere.

is_preview_deployments_enabled.reason: The creation endpoint answered HTTP 422 'This field is not allowed.' for this exact name, so the API neither accepts nor reports it.
is_preview_deployments_enabled.compensating_control: Preview deployments publish under a generated domain. fqdn is null, is verified as null on every reconcile, and a non-null fqdn fails the run, so a preview has no route to publish on.

is_force_https_enabled.compensating_control: Redirection only applies to a public route. The spec declares public_fqdn null and reconcile fails if an FQDN appears, so there is no HTTP route to redirect.

connect_to_docker_network.reason: Not reported on this version. Not writing it was wrong: the container was created detached from the shared network and the first readiness probe found neither alias resolvable, while reconcile reported PENDING-OWNER-UI as though a formality were outstanding. That diagnosis is now itself withdrawn: the container is attached and was attached all along, and the unresolvable names had a different cause.
connect_to_docker_network.compensating_control: Superseded five times. The first claimed reachability was proven by the Postgres connectivity check; that check proves the operations runner reaches Postgres and says nothing about this container. The second claimed the probe named in verified_by had confirmed the attachment; it had not, because gateway_readiness.py returns 'unknown' by design rather than a verdict, and run 31531842811 reported placement=runner_off_application_network - it declined to rule because the runner was off the applications' network, and a citation to an instrument that declines is not a verification. The third claimed attachment was proven because /ready opens a database connection from inside this container, so a 200 answered here (run 31542579590) required reaching the managed database over the shared network; the bridge still carries outbound IP connectivity, so that proved reachability and never proved attachment. Those three shared a shape: each inferred attachment from something a detached container can also do. The fourth claimed the opposite and was also wrong, in the mirror-image way: service-resolve measured this container directly (run 31583716911), localhost resolved and ai-gateway did not, and that was read as 'no embedded DNS, therefore the default bridge, therefore this API version accepts the field without applying it'. The fifth correction disproves the fourth by measurement. The census had no control: it asked for a name that could not have resolved on a working network either, because this application declared no network alias, so the rung tested two conditions and was reported as testing one. A control was added - a neighbour discovered at run time to declare its own name as an alias - and in run 31590576870, from inside this container, adapteng-baserow-adapter resolved to 10.0.1.11. A container on the default bridge cannot resolve a neighbour by name, so this container is on the shared user-defined network and its embedded DNS works. Nothing is or was wrong with the attachment. The real defect was the absence of custom_network_aliases, which is now declared in network.network_aliases, is reported by the API, and is therefore verified by read-back on every reconcile rather than written blind.
connect_to_docker_network.verified_by: scripts/coolify_deploy.py service-resolve, in .github/workflows/coolify-deploy.yml. It runs a name-resolution census inside this container, beginning with localhost, which needs no resolver, and then a control neighbour that declares its own name as a network alias. The control is what makes the census able to rule: if the control resolves and this container's own name does not, the network is sound and the name is missing, which are the two conditions the census previously ran together. Look for 'service-resolve ok', or 'reason=no_network_alias' which clears the network and names the alias as the fault.

configuration.note: The service image ends with ENV AI_GATEWAY_HTTP_HOST=127.0.0.1, and app/config.py falls back to the same loopback address. A process bound to loopback answers only callers inside its own container, so the container-network health probe and every internal caller would be refused and the deployment could never become healthy. Binding all interfaces is what makes the container reachable on the private network; nothing is published to the internet, because there is no public FQDN and no port mapping.
Declared so the listening port, the exposed port and the health-check port have exactly one source of truth in this file.
Must equal PRICE_VERSION in app/pricing.py. The service refuses to start on any other snapshot, so a stale value here is a startup failure, not a silent mispricing.
app/config.py refuses any lease at or below timeout*attempts + retry backoff + 15s. With the values above that floor is 75.5s, so 90 is the smallest round value that starts.

Not a secret and not an owner decision: it is already the committed repository variable GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT_ID on the platform repository and GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT on its approved-assets environments. app/config.py requires it with no default, so leaving it owner-held made a published identifier into a startup blocker.

externally_provided_configuration.reason: Caller authentication material. Never written to this repository; supplied to a reconcile run by reference and held in the Coolify environment store.

Connection string for the adapteng_ops budget ledger, carrying the ai_gateway_runtime password. Generated on the production host and posted to Coolify from there, so the password never reaches a runner, a log or this repository.

Operational data, not a secret and not a standing owner decision: the published ECB euro reference rate, inverted. Supplied at reconcile time from the AI_GATEWAY_FX_USD_EUR repository variable so refreshing the rate is one variable edit rather than a commit, and so a dated rate committed here can never be pushed back over a fresher one.
The reference date of the rate above, as an ISO-8601 timestamp with offset. Not sensitive, and deliberately visible in the reconcile log: the provenance is the audit evidence.
Provenance label naming the publication, its date and the published direction that was inverted, so a stored cost can be traced to the quote it used.

A filesystem path, not a credential. app/config.py fails closed at boot when it is set but does not name a readable file, so it is declared here rather than inline: it must be set only once the credential file is actually mounted, and never before.
